questions.q: Why shouldn't Power BI query a raw fact table directly, according to this lesson?
options: It forces every refresh or DirectQuery interaction to redo the same joins and aggregations from scratch, and exposes every column to potential report authors
Snowflake technically blocks Power BI from ever querying a fact table
Fact tables are always too small to be useful for BI reporting
There is no difference in performance or exposure between a fact table and a reporting view
questions.explain: A reporting view pre-shapes and pre-aggregates data specifically for what a dashboard needs, instead of re-deriving it from the raw fact table on every query.

questions.q: What does CREATE SECURE VIEW specifically protect against that an ordinary view does not?
options: It hides the view's definition from users without privileges on it and limits optimizer behaviors that could otherwise leak information about underlying data
It makes the view run faster than a materialized view in every case
It automatically encrypts all data in the underlying tables
It prevents the view from ever being queried by Power BI
questions.explain: SECURE views hide their definition and limit information leakage through query plans/optimizer behavior — appropriate for anything meant to expose a summary, not raw rows.

questions.q: What is the key limitation of Snowflake materialized views mentioned in this lesson?
options: They only support a single underlying table — no joins — which rules them out for most fact-and-dimension reporting views
They can only be created by the ACCOUNTADMIN role
They cannot include any aggregate functions like SUM or COUNT
They are automatically dropped every 24 hours
questions.explain: Materialized views only support a single table, so a reporting view that joins fact and dimension tables can't use one directly.

questions.q: What is the recommended alternative when a reporting view needs to join fact and dimension tables but a materialized view can't be used?
options: A scheduled Task that writes the join's pre-aggregated result into a physical summary table
Abandoning the join and only reporting on the fact table alone
Switching Power BI to Import mode automatically fixes this
There is no workaround — joined reporting views are impossible in Snowflake
questions.explain: A scheduled Task can run the join on a cadence and persist the result to a physical summary table, trading some freshness for near-zero query cost.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the three performance levers this lesson highlights for BI query patterns?
options: Clustering keys on the columns dashboards filter on most, such as a date column
Disabling result caching to force fresh computation every time
Always using the largest available warehouse size regardless of query pattern
Removing all views and querying only raw tables for speed
questions.explain: Clustering keys help Snowflake prune micro-partitions to the relevant range, alongside result caching and a right-sized reporting warehouse.
